Starting a project

K.A. Stam

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/starting_a_project.Rmd
starting_a_project.Rmd

A FAIRground is the combination of three things: a structured directory on disk, a SQL database, and a set of R ETL scripts that move data from raw files into the database. This guide shows how to create each of them from scratch.

1. Create the project directory 

startProject(dir = dir)
list.files(dir)
#> [1] "analyses"             "beFAIR_project.Rproj" "codebooks"           
#> [4] "common"               "experiments"          "fairground.yml"      
#> [7] "logs"                 "studies"

startProject() creates the standard FAIRground layout:

Folder Purpose
studies/ Clinical trial metadata — participants, arms, design
experiments/ Laboratory measurements (CyTOF, ELISA, Olink, …)
analyses/ Derived results computed from study and experiment data
common/ Shared reference files
codebooks/ Custom YAML codebooks for project-specific tables
logs/ JSON run logs written by databaseUpdate()

2. Connect and initialise the database 

con <- FAIRgroundConnect(drv = RSQLite::SQLite(), dsn = ":memory:")
databaseInitialize()
DBI::dbListTables(con)
#> [1] "HGNC"             "LUNC"             "table_codebook"   "table_datasource"
#> [5] "table_dependency" "table_project"    "table_script"

databaseInitialize() creates the registry tables that beFAIR uses to track codebook versions (table_codebook) and ETL scripts (table_script). You only run this once when setting up a new database.

In production you would connect via a DSN: FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN"). On Windows, configure DSNs in the ODBC Data Sources administrator.

3. Register a study 

addStudy(study_name = "MyStudy", study_id = "MYST1")
list.files("studies/MyStudy")
#> [1] "data"      "meta.yaml" "scripts"

addStudy() creates a folder under studies/ and drafts the four mandatory ETL scripts:

list.files("studies/MyStudy/scripts")
#> [1] "id_mapping.R"  "participant.R" "studyarm.R"    "studydesign.R"
Script What it populates
id_mapping.R Maps raw source IDs to pseudonymous participant_id values
participant.R One row per participant — demographics, enrolment, BMI
studyarm.R The study arms (control, treatment groups, dosing cohorts)
studydesign.R Scheduled timepoints and events in the trial protocol

Each script is a template: the codebook structure and boilerplate are pre-filled, and you complete the data-mapping logic for your specific raw files. See Adding a study for a full walkthrough of each script.

4. Fill in the study metadata

addStudy() also creates a meta.yaml file with fields you should complete:

#> study_id: MYST1
#> name: MyStudy
#> title: ~
#> study_organism: ~
#> disease: ~
#> pathogen: ~
#> facilities: ~
#> cities: ~
#> countries: ~
#> geopoints: ~
#> principal_investigator: ~
#> contact_name: ~
#> contact_email: ~
#> primary_outcome: ~
#> summary: ~
#> description: ~
#> actual_start_date: ~
#> actual_completion_date: ~
#> actual_enrollment: ~
#> registration_link: ~
#> pbmc_location_file: ~
#> pbmc_location_vials: ~
#> pbmc_contact: ~

If the study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, pass the registration code and beFAIR will pre-fill the relevant metadata automatically:

addStudy(study_name = "MyStudy", study_id = "MYST1",
         registration_code = "NCT02237586")

5. Run the update

Once your ETL scripts are complete, databaseUpdate() runs them all, validates the output, and loads the results:

databaseUpdate()

You re-run this command whenever scripts change or new data arrives. beFAIR detects which scripts have changed (via MD5 hash), skips anything unchanged, and only reloads what is new or updated.
